title: Fastify Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: A Fastify handler can return a value directly. Open GET /. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Fastify sends the returned string as the route response. async lets the handler return through a promise. Return the result or send it with reply; do not do both.

exercises.question: Fastify turns a returned object into JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The returned JavaScript object is serialised as JSON with its two fields. Return data, not a hand-built JSON string, when possible.

exercises.question: A colon marks a path parameter. GET /hello/Ravi puts the name in request.params. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: request.params.name contains Ravi. That value is inserted into the returned string. Path values are text unless a schema converts and validates them.

exercises.question: Query input follows the question mark. GET /search?q=cat reads q. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: request.query.q holds cat. The type check accepts it and creates the term field. Check query values rather than assuming they are always strings.

exercises.question: Fastify can parse JSON bodies. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The JSON parser provides the body object. A valid title reaches the 201 response. Content-Type tells the server how to read the body.

exercises.question: A schema describes allowed data. GET /books/3 converts and checks id as a positive integer. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The integer schema converts and checks the path input. The handler receives numeric id 3. Schemas must describe the input shape you actually expect.

exercises.question: A preHandler hook runs before the route handler. GET / uses the request field set by the hook. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: decorateRequest declares the field. The hook fills it before the route reads it. Use async hooks or callback hooks consistently; do not mix both styles.

exercises.question: decorate adds a named helper to the Fastify instance. GET / uses that helper. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: decorate adds greet to the app instance. The route calls it with Ravi. Register the helper before the route uses it.

exercises.question: register gives a plugin its own scope. A prefix puts its routes under /api. Open GET /api/books. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The plugin owns /books under its /api prefix, so the combined route matches. The plugin prefix is part of the final URL.

exercises.question: A response schema can choose which fields are sent. GET /book keeps title and leaves out internalNote. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The response schema lists title only. Fastify serialises that public field and omits the note. A response schema is not a replacement for deciding which data is safe to return.

exercises.question: setErrorHandler handles errors from routes. GET /broken returns a simple public message. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The thrown error reaches the configured handler, which sends status 500 and a short message. Avoid showing private stack traces to clients.

exercises.question: inject runs a request inside Fastify. This example prints the response body and closes the app without listening. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: inject executes GET /score in memory. response.body is the JSON string from that route. Close the app after tests so resources are released.
